CWE-14.name: Compiler Removal of Code to Clear Buffers
CWE-14.question: Does this function wipe a buffer holding a secret with a plain store or memset that an optimising compiler may drop because the buffer is never read again?

any: a buffer holding a key, password, token or other secret is overwritten just before it is freed, goes out of scope or the function returns, and nothing reads it afterwards
c: memset, bzero or a hand-written zeroing loop on a local or soon-freed secret buffer, with no volatile access, barrier or secure-clear API
cpp: std::fill, memset, clear() or assigning an empty value is applied to a std::string or std::vector secret just before it is destroyed; clear() overwrites nothing

any: the buffer does not hold sensitive data
the buffer is read or passed on after it is cleared
c: the wipe uses memset_s, explicit_bzero, SecureZeroMemory, OPENSSL_cleanse or a similar clear that the compiler must keep
the wipe writes through a volatile pointer or is followed by a compiler barrier

CWE-325.name: Missing Cryptographic Step
CWE-325.question: Does this function leave out a step its cryptographic operation needs, such as verifying a tag, using a fresh IV or salt, or checking a signature result?

any: authenticated decryption output is used without verifying the tag, or a MAC or signature is computed but its comparison result is ignored
a block cipher is used in a chaining mode with a zero, constant or reused IV or nonce
a password is hashed without a salt or with a single fast hash where a key-derivation step is expected
a key exchange or handshake omits verifying the peer's public key, certificate or signature
c: EVP_DecryptFinal_ex or a verify call's return value is not checked before the plaintext is trusted

any: a high-level library call performs the full construction, such as an AEAD open that fails on a bad tag, or a password-hashing function with built-in salt
every verification result is checked and failure stops processing
IVs or nonces come from a secure random source or a never-repeating counter per key

distinguish_from.CWE-327: every step is present but the algorithm itself is broken or risky

CWE-777.name: Regular Expression without Anchors
CWE-777.question: Does this function validate or filter a string with a regular expression that is not anchored at both ends, so extra content before or after the match is accepted?

any: a regular expression used to accept or reject input lacks ^ and $ (or \A and \z) and is applied with a search-style call
an allowlist pattern is anchored at only one end
javascript: RegExp.test() or String.match() validates input with a pattern lacking ^...$
python: re.search() or re.match() is used for validation with no $ or \Z at the end of the pattern

any: the regular expression is used to find, extract or replace text rather than to validate or authorise input
the pattern is anchored at both ends, or applied with a whole-string call
rust: Regex::is_match on a pattern wrapped in ^...$

distinguish_from.CWE-1333: the concern is catastrophic backtracking rather than what the pattern accepts
